Company Overview
We design, manufacture, and distribute fiber connectivity, fiber protection, fiber management, power delivery, and fiber sensing solutions that enable rapid and cost-effective deployment of fiber-based networks for telecommunications, data centers, wireless communications, and critical infrastructure, primarily across North America. Our “fiber to anywhere” platform serves the diverse needs of Community Broadband customers (Tier 2 and 3 telco carriers, utilities, municipalities, and alternative carriers); Multiple System Operators (cable television providers); Large Regional Service Providers (incumbent local exchange carriers operating multistate networks with more than 500,000 subscribers); National Carriers (Tier 1 wireline and wireline/wireless communications carriers); International customers (primarily in Canada, the Caribbean, Central and South America, and Mexico); Data Center customers (hyperscale, colocation, and service provider-owned data centers); and Enterprise and Edge customers.
Our mission is to enable the lifestyle benefits that better broadband and connectivity provides through innovative product designs that accelerate fiber-based deployment, making communications networks simpler and more affordable to build, power, and operate. Broadband remains our core market. At the same time, network architectures continue to evolve and converge as computing, storage, and artificial intelligence workloads expand across data centers of all sizes, including regional and edge facilities operated by broadband service providers. These evolving networks require greater fiber density, power to remote sites, and continuous monitoring of physical infrastructure.
We believe our modular, craft-friendly design approach, built around the Clearview® Cassette and expanded through our NOVA™ platform, combined with our manufacturing operations in the U.S. and Mexico and our ability to respond quickly to customer needs, position us to serve these adjacent markets. Our focus remains on helping customers reduce costs and accelerate fiber deployment wherever connectivity is needed.
Segment Information
We conduct operations globally and currently operate as one operating segment and one reportable segment.
On November 11, 2025, the Company completed the sale of its Nestor Cables business, which was previously reported as a separate operating segment. As a result of the sale, the historical operating results of the Nestor Cables business have been classified as discontinued operations in the Company's consolidated financial statements. The assets and liabilities associated with the discontinued business were classified as held for sale in the applicable prior-period consolidated balance sheet.
Clearfield is focused on providing fiber management, fiber protection, fiber delivery, power delivery, and fiber sensing products that accelerate the deployment and turn-up of fiber-based networks serving residential homes, businesses, data centers, wireless sites, and other network infrastructure. We offer a broad portfolio of products designed to help service providers and network operators build fiber networks more efficiently, meet service delivery demands, and align networks construction costs with customer take rates.
Clearfield’s products are designed to help customers accelerate Fiber to the Home (“FTTH”) deployments by reducing the labor, time, and resources required to connect homes. Our products also help service providers accelerate time to revenue in Multiple Dwelling Units (“MDUs”) and Multiple Tenant Units (“MTUs”) by reducing the labor and materials required to deliver gigabit services. In business applications, our solutions help improve service profitability through faster building access, simplified network reconfiguration, and quicker service activation. In data centers, our modular high-density platform is designed to reduce cable preparation, routing complexity, and splicing time in space-constrained environments. Additionally, our products support wireless 4G and 5G network deployments by simplifying fiber management, improving test access and fiber protection, and enabling power delivery to remote edge sites.
Substantially all final product assembly is performed at Clearfield’s manufacturing facilities in Brooklyn Park, Minnesota and Tijuana, Mexico, with support from a network of domestic and international manufacturing partners. Clearfield’s manufacturing capabilities provide the flexibility to meet customer requirements through both quick-turn production and scheduled delivery arrangements.
Products
Our product strategy focuses on evaluating evolving technologies and customer requirements across broadband communications, data centers, and network infrastructure to develop innovative, high-quality products that simplify network design, installation, and operation. We are committed to making fiber deployment success easier by providing craft-friendly, pre-connectorized plug-and-play fiber assemblies, fiber management and pathway, power, and sensing products to speed deployments and provide the lowest total cost of ownership for our customer’s networks. These solutions are designed to accelerate network deployments, reduce installation complexity, and lower the total cost of ownership for our customers.
Throughout the fiber deployment process, from the Inside Plant (“ISP”) through the Outside Plant (“OSP”), and access network to the final fiber connection at the home, business, data center or other location, our labor-saving solutions help service providers address network design and installation challenges. Our products are designed to simplify network engineering and installation, reducing the time, labor, and technical expertise required to deploy fiber networks.
By utilizing factory-terminated single-fiber and multi-fiber plug-and-play connectors, our solutions help service providers increase deployment efficiency and accelerate the number of homes passed and connected. Factory-terminated, low-loss connectors also support consistent optical performance while reducing the need for field termination and splicing.
Our innovative slack storage spools and deployment reels reduce the need for precise field cable measurements, whether within network cabinets or at customer premises. These solutions enable the use of standardized, double-ended cable assemblies rather than relying on custom-built cable lengths or multiple field splicing operations, helping reduce installation time and complexity.
Our product development activities are conducted primarily internally, supplemented by collaboration with customers and technology partners. We believe that broadband communications, data center, and network infrastructure technologies will continue to evolve, and our success depends in part on our ability to anticipate and respond to changing customer requirements and technological advancements. Research and development expenses are included in selling, general and administrative expenses in our consolidated statements of operations.
Some of our products currently offered are described below.
FieldSmart ® is a series of panels, cabinets, wall boxes and other enclosures that provide a consistent design from the inside plant of the telco’s “central office” or cable television’s head-end, all the way through the outside plant to the access network to within the home or business. The Clearview Cassette is the core building block of every product within the FieldSmart fiber management system. Clearview configuration options support tool-less installation, in-cassette buffer tube/ribbon slack storage as well as front access-only designs. The small footprint reduces costs and improves density without compromising critical design elements of access, bend-radius protection, physical fiber protection and route path diversity. All types of fiber cable construction can be integrated within the cassette to support all patch only, patch and splice (in-cassette splicing), passive optical component hardware and plug-and-play scenarios.
WaveSmart ® optical components are integrated for signal coupling, splitting, termination, multiplexing, demultiplexing and attenuation for a seamless integration within our fiber management platform. The products are built and tested for harsh environments to meet industry standards, ensuring customers performance in extreme outside plant conditions.
Active Cabinets using our FiberFlex™ product lines feature either fully integrated, fully engineered cabinets equipped with specific active electronics configurations or universal cabinets ready for mounting other electronic equipment. This product line features Clearfield’s fiber management solutions housing the Clearview Cassette. The FieldSmart FiberFlex product line of outdoor active cabinets features multiple sizes for universal configurations of electronic equipment.
CraftSmart ® FiberFirst ™ pedestals are designed to support fiber-only networks.

Risks Relating to Our Operations
We depend on the availability of sufficient supply of certain materials. Global disruptions in the supply chain for these materials could prevent us from meeting customer demand for our products.
We purchase critical components for our products, including injection molded parts, various cabling, optical components, components for active cabinets, and connectors from third parties, some of which are single- or limited-source suppliers. We depend on the ability of these third-party suppliers to secure a sufficient supply of raw materials and maintain sufficient manufacturing and shipping capacity. The global supply chain for raw materials critical to our products has in the past, and may again in the future, suffer shortages, shipping delays and shipping shortages. This may lead some manufacturers who depend on these raw materials to experience shortages, delivery delays and price increases for both the raw materials and shipping, with the corresponding consequence that these manufacturers may be delayed in delivering products to us or may charge higher prices for these products, or there may be increased shipping costs associated with the products. Some manufacturers may also allocate short supply of products among Clearfield and their other customers. The current supply constraints of optical fiber, cable and connectors driven by the rapid rise in demand for artificial intelligence (“AI”) and cloud computing, raw material constraints, manufacturing capacity limits, and logistics have led to extended lead times, increased exposure to allocation decisions, higher product costs, and delays in customer deployments and buildouts.
Increased demand for the Company’s products from its customers may put pressure on the Company’s supply chain, particularly during periods of disruption in the global supply chain and may lead to increases in costs or delays in obtaining the materials and components for our products from our suppliers. The Company’s ability to recognize revenue in the future for customer orders will depend on our ability to manufacture and deliver products to the customers and fulfill other contractual obligations. Our ability to meet future customer demand for our products will in turn depend upon our suppliers receiving timely and adequate supplies of raw materials to be able to produce the critical materials and components they supply to us. Although we place a high value on long-term relationships with our suppliers, generally we do not have long-term supply contracts but instead conduct business on an order-by-order basis. Therefore, we also compete with other companies for the production capacity of manufacturers of the materials and components we need for our products. We also are exposed to potentially increasing costs associated with the materials and components we purchase from suppliers or increased costs associated with shipping generally. We may attempt to mitigate the effect of increases in our cost of goods sold through sourcing or stocking initiatives and by selectively increasing the prices of our products. However, we may be unable to fully pass on these costs to our customers. Long lead times for certain components and changes in demand for our products may impact our ability to accurately forecast our production requirements. As a result, certain component inventory purchases may become excess or obsolete, which could have an adverse effect on our financial condition and results of operations.
The reduction of available production capacity among our suppliers, their failures to meet production deadlines or increases to us in their manufacturing or shipping costs may impact our ability to deliver quality products to our customers on a timely basis, make our products less competitive due to extended delivery times or increased price, negatively impact our customer or distributor relationships, and result in lower net sales and profit. Any delays or inabilities in meeting customer required shipping dates may also expose us to order cancellations in our sales order backlog by customers, which could have an adverse effect on our results of operations.
We rely on single-source suppliers, which could cause delays, increases in costs, or prevent us from completing customer orders, all of which could materially harm our business.
We assemble our products using materials and components supplied by various subcontractors and suppliers. We purchase critical components for our products, including injection molded parts, various cabling, optical components, and connectors from third parties, some of whom are single- or limited-source suppliers. If any of our suppliers are unable to ship critical components, we may be unable to manufacture and ship products to our distributors or customers. If the price of these components increases for any reason, or if these suppliers are unable or unwilling to deliver, we may have to find another source, which could result in interruptions, increased costs, delays, lost sales, and quality control problems.
Further, the costs to obtain certain raw materials and supplies, such as fiber, are subject to price fluctuations, which may be substantial, because of global market demands. Many companies utilize the same raw materials and supplies in the production of their products as we use in our products. Companies with more resources than us may have a competitive advantage in obtaining raw materials and supplies due to greater purchasing power. Some raw materials or supplies may be subject to regulatory actions, which may affect available supplies. Further, new or increased tariffs may be imposed by governments on imports from other countries that are the single- or limited-source of our materials and components. Tariffs increase the cost of the materials and components that go into making our products, but we are generally unable to pass some or all of these increased costs on to our customers. Accordingly, these increased costs adversely impact the gross margin that we earn on our products. Furthermore, due to general economic conditions in the U.S. and globally, our suppliers may experience financial difficulties, which could result in increased delays, additional costs, or loss of a supplier.
The termination or interruption of any of these relationships, or the failure of these manufacturers or suppliers to supply components or raw materials to us on a timely basis or in sufficient quantities, likely would cause us to be unable to meet orders for our products and harm our reputation and our business. Identifying and qualifying alternative suppliers would take time, involve significant additional costs, and may delay the production of our products. If we fail to forecast our manufacturing requirements accurately or fail to properly manage our inventory with our contract manufacturers, we could incur additional costs, experience manufacturing delays, and lose sales.
